candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction
support_spans: intermittent chest pain over 10 days and heavy chest pain lasting for 3 hours in the previous 5 days
ECG showed abnormal Q wave and ST-segment elevation with terminal T-wave inversion in leads II, III, and aVF
Mildly elevated cardiac enzymes (creatine kinase: 237 U/L)
High-sensitivity troponin I: 3348 pg/mL
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and test results, including ECG changes and elevated cardiac enzymes, are consistent with a myocardial infarction.

candidates.name: Inferior Wall Myocardial Infarction
support_spans: inferior-posterior left ventricular wall akinesis with small pericardial effusion
Thrombotic obstruction in right coronary artery
candidates.why: The location of the wall akinesis and the thrombotic obstruction in the right coronary artery suggest an inferior wall myocardial infarction.

candidates.name: Ventricular Aneurysm
support_spans: Large aneurysm formation with myocardial defect (3 cm diameter) in inferior wall
candidates.why: The echocardiography and cardiac CT angiography results show a large aneurysm formation in the inferior wall, which is a complication of a myocardial infarction.
